title: function-calling parse debug scratchpad (maya)
content:
Summary:
Quick scratchpad tracking the investigation of intermittent JSON/structured-output parse failures when using function/tool calling in user integrations. Reproduces locally, inconsistent between model variants and streaming vs non-streaming. Notes, commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps below.

Context:
- Issue reported by customer on Dedicated: function-calling responses sometimes include malformed JSON or extra tokens that break the downstream parser. Customer sees errors ~1-2% of requests for a single route.
- Initial triage: not obviously prompt-related (same prompt mostly OK), occurs across a few model variants (open-llama-70b, redwood-v1-small), more frequent with higher max_tokens and streaming enabled.

Reproduction attempts (local):
1) Baseline request (non-streaming):
  - curl -> Redwood hosted endpoint (dev account)
  - Prompt: "Call tool get_order with args {order_id}"
  - Function schema (example):
    name: get_order
    parameters: {"type": "object", "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["order_id"]}

curl command used:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"get_order 12345"}],"functions":[{"name":"get_order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"get_order"}}'

Outcome: 99/100 requests returned well-formed JSON in the function call response. 1/100 returned: "{\"order_id\": 12345}" (order_id as number) which fails strict schema validation (expecting string).

2) Streaming vs non-streaming:
  - Tried streaming (chunked SSE) and non-streaming. Streaming had slightly higher failure rate (approx 1.8% vs 1.0%). Observed partial chunks with trailing commas sometimes present in final assembled payload when client reassembly code is naive.
  - Verified client reassembly (my test harness) was correctly concatenating event.data lines; I still see a few malformed tokens before finalization.

3) Model variant influence:
  - redwood-v1-small: baseline above.
  - redwood-v1-medium: slightly lower failure rate.
  - open-llama-70b: higher failure rate but also observed different tokenization (quotes vs no quotes).
  - hypothesis: some models prefer numeric literal for numeric-looking strings unless schema enforces quoting in generation.

Error snippets (captured from logs):
  - "Failed to parse function args JSON: Unexpected token 1 in JSON at position 13"
  - "ValidationError: order_id must be a string (received number)"
  - Raw function call text: '{order_id: 12345}'
  - Raw function call text: '"{\"order_id\": 12345}"' (wrapped as string)
  - Streaming chunk example:
      data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"function_call":{"name":"get_order","arguments":"{\\\"order_id\\\": 12345"}}}}]
      data: [DONE]
    Note: the arguments field arrived as a JSON string inside the JSON payload (escaped) which required an extra parse step; sometimes double-escaped on server side.

Commands/logs tried to debug server-side:
- Reproduced with request_id=dev-20260224-01. Logged entire response payloads (pre and post any server-side normalization) to see when escaping happened.
- grep logs for request_id and tracked the sequence: model output (tokens) -> assemble -> postprocess (ensure args is object) -> emit.
- Observed that the postprocess step attempts to json.parse and falls back to a regex if parse fails. Fallback used on ~1% and returned numeric without quotes.

Hypotheses so far:
1) Model tokenization/formatting variance causes numeric-looking strings to be emitted as unquoted numbers when schema doesn't strictly coerce types. Some LLMs prefer unquoted numeric literals.
2) Streaming concat/reassembly edge cases: partial chunk boundaries sometimes split inside escape sequences, producing temporary invalid JSON that some server-side parsers attempt to salvage incorrectly (regex replace), introducing subtle bugs.
3) Double-escaping: platform postprocess may accidentally stringify arguments (e.g., JSON.stringify applied twice) under certain code paths (especially when function_call.arguments is detected as a string by the model). When we then attempt JSON.parse we get a string that contains JSON, leading to inconsistent handling.
4) Customer payload variability: sometimes order_id includes leading zeros or non-numeric chars; model may choose to output unquoted when it thinks numeric is correct.

What I've tried (server-side fixes & tests):
- Force-parse path: if arguments is a string, try JSON.parse once, if that yields string, try JSON.parse again (to handle double-serialized). Logged counts: double-serialized occurred ~0.1% of failures.
- Strict coercion: after parse, coerce types according to schema (e.g., convert numbers -> strings for order_id if type=string). This fixes customer but feels brittle and may mask legit type errors.
- Reject-and-retry: on parse/validation fail, automatically retry the request with temperature=0 and max_tokens smaller. Reduced failure rate but impacted latency and throughput.
- Streaming buffer improvements: implemented more conservative chunk-assembly logic to handle escape sequences across boundaries. Some improvement (~30% reduction in streaming-specific failures).

Open questions / TODO:
- Should platform enforce strict JSON quoting for function_call.arguments (always return as JSON object and never as string)? Pros: deterministic for integrators. Cons: might require heavy canonicalization and could affect LLM generation behavior.
- If we coerce types (numbers->strings), we hide model mistakes. Do we prefer to fail fast and surface to customers or to auto-fix? Need product guidance.
- Investigate model generation prompts: can we add a stronger assistant system message instructing model to always output arguments as JSON with strings for certain fields? Quick test: added explicit schema description in system prompt 94 reduced numeric coercion for redwood-v1-small in controlled tests.

Immediate next steps (short-term):
1) Add additional logging to capture raw token stream + postprocess diff for failing requests (ticketed and gated at 1% sampling).
2) Ship streaming buffer fix and monitor error rate for 48h.
3) Add an optional server-side safe-coercion toggle per-route (opt-in) so customers can enable tolerant behavior while we decide on default.
4) Create a small eval harness to run 1000 synthetic requests across model variants with variations in order_id formatting (leading zeros, hyphens, long string) to characterize failure modes.
5) Product question: propose default behavior: fail-fast with clear error vs tolerant-coerce. Draft note for PMs.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Check PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 for postprocess regex -> we may need to replace fallback with a stricter state-machine that doesn't mangle numeric tokens.
- Cross-check with client SDK teams: ensure JS SDK reassembly isn't silently responsible (we already verified local harness but coordinate with @sdk-team).
- Capture example of offending model token stream (save to S3) for RLHF/retraining triggers if pattern persistent.

Breadcrumbs / timeline:
- 2026-02-20: customer first reported route failing intermittently.
- 2026-02-21: quick triage; suspected SDK reassembly.
- 2026-02-22: reproduced locally; narrowed to function_call.arguments payload formatting.
- 2026-02-24: started server-side instrumentation and temporary coercion fix.
- 2026-02-28: implemented streaming buffer improvements for escape handling.
- 2026-03-02: observed reduced failures; still planning eval harness + product decision.

Appendix: quick example pairs (bad vs good)
- Bad: {order_id: 12345}  -> invalid JSON (keys unquoted)
- Bad: "{\"order_id\": 12345}" -> double-stringified, needs extra parse
- Good (expected): {"order_id": "12345"} -> valid and matches schema

Contact: ping me (maya.patel@redwood.ai) or DM Liam for immediate debug pairing.

End of scratchpad.
